title: Group conversation treatment for aphasia
text: Group conversation treatment improves communication and wellbeing for people with chronic aphasia and reduces isolation. Structured, topic-based groups give repeated, meaningful practice that one-to-one sessions alone do not, and can be run by trained volunteers with professional support.
source: Elman RJ, Bernstein-Ellis E. The efficacy of group communication treatment in adults with chronic aphasia. J Speech Lang Hear Res 42(2):411–419

title: Life participation approach
text: The Life Participation Approach to Aphasia judges success by re-engagement in chosen life activities and conversation, not test scores alone. Reminiscence and everyday topics — food, songs, journeys, festivals — give people something real to talk about and belong to.
source: Chapey R, et al. Life participation approach to aphasia. ASHA Leader

title: Reminiscence and singing
text: Familiar songs and reminiscence draw on well-preserved memory and melody. Many people with non-fluent aphasia can sing words they cannot speak, so singing together lowers the barrier to joining in and lifts mood.
source: Tamplin J, Baker FA. Music engagement and wellbeing in neurorehabilitation.

title: Running a group for members with hearing loss
text: In a group, members with hearing loss do best when only one person speaks at a time, the room is quiet, faces are visible and the topic is named. Keep background music low and pause often to check everyone is following.
source: Ida Institute — group communication and person-centred care
